data.title: J Infratech files IPO papers; eyes ₹600 cr via fresh issue
data.description:
J Infratech Ltd, an integrated infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) firm, has filed preliminary papers with the market regulator Sebi for an initial public offering (IPO) comprising a fresh issue of shares worth ₹600 crore.

Apart from the fresh issue, the company's proposed IPO comprises an offer for sale (OFS) of 1 crore equity shares by promoters, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed on Friday.

The Haryana-based company may also consider a pre-IPO placement of up to ₹120 crore. In case the placement is completed, the size of the fresh issue will be reduced accordingly.

The proceeds from the IPO will primarily be utilised to meet working capital requirements, repay or pre-pay certain borrowings and for general corporate purposes.

J Infratech is an integrated infrastructure engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company focused on roads, highways and bridges, with experience in executing large-scale road development projects involving specialised structures across India.

The company commenced operations in 2005 through its partnership firm, Jandu Construction Co, which was subsequently converted into J Infratech in 2019.

As of July 31, 2026, the company had completed 35 projects and was executing 46 projects across 16 states and three Union Territories.

The equity shares proposed to be offered through the IPO are proposed to be listed on both BSE and NSE.

Systematix Corporate Services is the book-running lead manager to the issue, and KFin Technologies is the registrar to the offer.

data.title: Microsoft Copilot Is Turning Into An ‘AI Operating System’ — Here’s What It Means For MSFT Stock, According To Oppenheimer’s Brian Schwartz
data.description:
Key points:
  • Schwartz said Microsoft’s latest Copilot developments transform the product from a standalone chatbot into what he described as an “AI operating system.”
  • He added that this shift is significant because operating systems and platforms can drive higher user engagement, create more monetization opportunities and build greater customer stickiness.
  • Schwartz said that if Azure growth approaches 50% while operating at a scale exceeding $100 billion, that could drive a rerating of Microsoft stock.

Oppenheimer analyst Brian Schwartz says Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) is moving deeper into the artificial intelligence race following its latest Copilot announcement, which he believes strengthens the software giant’s investment case.

During an interview with CNBC, Schwartz said Microsoft’s Copilot announcement changes the narrative around the company as investors continue to search for clear winners in the AI era.

“Microsoft is a top pick for us. Today's announcement from Microsoft was substantial. Today's announcement helps push them deeper into that AI win category,” he said.

Microsoft shares closed 4% higher in Friday’s regular trade, while edging up by 0.3% in the after-hours session.

MSFT Copilot Becomes An ‘AI Operating System’

Schwartz said Microsoft’s latest Copilot developments transform the product from a standalone chatbot into what he described as an “AI operating system.”

He added that this shift is significant because operating systems and platforms can drive higher user engagement, create more monetization opportunities and build greater customer stickiness.

“When you're an operating system, when you're a platform provider, that leads to higher engagement, greater monetization opportunities and stickiness, and defensibility against competition,” Schwartz said.

MSFT Gets Clearer Path To Monetizing AI Usage

Schwartz said investors he spoke with were also focused on a clearer path for Microsoft to monetize heavy AI usage.

New capabilities including Cowork, co-development and Autopilot could be monetized through consumption-based pricing, credits and tokens, he said.

Under the model, users could pay a monthly subscription for routine tasks while more compute-intensive workloads generate additional consumption revenue.

Schwartz said that could create incremental growth opportunities for Microsoft 365 and Azure, supporting his expectation of business acceleration over the coming quarters.

Azure Growth Could Drive MSFT Stock Rerating, Says Schwartz

Schwartz also pointed to Azure and Microsoft 365 as the two businesses investors are watching most closely.

He said Azure is currently growing in the low-40% range and is expected to accelerate toward the mid-40% range in the current quarter. If Azure growth approaches 50% while operating at a scale exceeding $100 billion, Schwartz said that could drive a rerating of Microsoft stock.

He also highlighted Microsoft’s shift toward working with multiple AI model providers, including OpenAI and Anthropic, as part of its strategy to expand Copilot beyond traditional workplace use cases.

According to TheFly, Oppenheimer raised its price target for Microsoft to $570 from $515, while keeping an ‘Outperform’ rating. The new price target implies an upside potential of over 10% from Friday’s closing price.

What Retail Investors Think Of MSFT Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Microsoft trended in the ‘bullish’ territory, with message volumes at ‘high’ levels at the time of writing.

MSFT stock is up 7% year-to-date and 2% over the past 12 months. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 21% over the past 12 months, while the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK) is up 36%.

data.title: Meta turned Muse into a viral hit. Now comes the hard part.
data.description:
By Christine Ji

Meta is quickly racking up downloads for its Muse AI assistant, but the next step for Mark Zuckerberg is getting users to make the agent part of their everyday routines

Meta recently unveiled a new lineup of AI-integrated hardware including new Ray Bans and a keychain-sized Muse Charm.

For the past week, Meta's artificial-intelligence assistant Muse has sat at the top of Apple's U.S. App Store charts.

The widespread popularity of the agent - a fuzzy customizable avatar capable of sending emails, booking reservations, making online purchases and more - has sent shares of Meta (META) on a tear. The stock is up 31% since the beginning of the month.

But in a cutthroat AI ecosystem, no agent or application can afford to get too comfortable. As other companies race to push out new models and products, Meta will need to translate Muse's initial buzz into an everyday consumer habit to stay in the lead. Can the social-media giant shape the next generation of user behavior?

According to a Thursday report from Sensor Tower, Muse has accumulated over 3.4 million downloads across the U.S. and Canada since its Sept. 8 launch. The report also highlighted that Grok Bot, SpaceX's (SPCX) multi-agent platform, has picked up 2.2 million downloads since its August launch. Another AI assistant, Instinct, has risen in popularity recently as well.

Morningstar analyst Malik Ahmed Khan believes that Meta has an unique advantage in growing its Muse platform given its existing distribution with Instagram, Facebook and WhatsApp. With the exception of Alphabet's (GOOGL) (GOOG) Google, "Meta is the only company that has experience scaling multiple platforms to multi-billion-user levels," Khan told MarketWatch.

Muse gives Meta a direct window into user habits which can help future product development, Khan added. The company has identified nearly 400 "musecases" ranging from auditing unnecessary subscriptions to negotiating parking tickets.

JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth was further encouraged by the company's path forward following Wednesday's Meta Connect 2026 developer conference. Meta announced the third generation of its flagship Ray-Ban smart glasses, its first camera-free audio glasses, lightweight Meta VR glasses and the keychain-sized Muse Charm. All of these devices are compatible with Muse through voice capabilities.

"Muse represents the centerpiece of Meta's AI vision," Anmuth wrote, citing Meta's expanding hardware and software ecosystem. Muse is also accessible through an increasing number of third-party connectors such as Walmart (WMT), Instacart (CART), Box (BOX) and Wayfair (W).

"We continue to believe this is the first of many steps to bring tens and potentially hundreds of millions of businesses onto Muse, and form the foundation for monetization," Anmuth said of Muse's e-commerce partnerships.

Meta also needs to prove that AI agents can achieve widespread adoption among everyday people. Muse Charm, a small hardware device that allows users to query Muse without a phone, could help the agent become a seamless part of people's everyday lives.

Muse Charm "gives Meta another access point to its growing AI ecosystem, complementing products such as its AI glasses and its broader suite of apps and service," Counterpoint principal analyst Anshika Jain wrote in a Thursday note. Still, Jain cautioned that its success hinges on offering enough utility to justify carrying an extra device.

There's also the question of security and privacy. In order for an agent to take actions on a user's behalf, it needs access to sensitive personal data such as email accounts, payment credentials and third-party logins.

Security concerns remain an issue for companies across the industry, according to Urday Cheruvu, portfolio manager at Harding Loevner. "I'm not sure the trust is there for anyone, the reason being that this is so early and so new," Cheruvu told MarketWatch.

Meta has taken steps to ensure user privacy. Each user's Muse agent runs in a dedicated computer in the cloud called Muse Secure VM. Meta said it doesn't share any data from Muse with its core ad business. Later this year, Meta plans to roll out Muse Confidential VM, an upgraded security model that encrypts all user conversations and data behind a private key inaccessible even to Meta itself.

For now, Muse usage is "skewed among early adopters," Cheruvu said. But Cheruvu expects Meta to promote different Muse use cases on Instagram Reels and its other platforms, boosting adoption and creating a barrier to entry for competitors.

"Muse is connected to Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram," Cheruvu said. "It already knows so much...so it can anticipate what you want better."

-Christine Ji

This content was created by MarketWatch, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. MarketWatch is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: In Brazil, frustration over cost of living undermines Lula's reelection bid
data.description:
Key points:
  • Candidate Flavio has blamed President Lula for high cost of living
  • Economists say years of price hikes weigh on voters, despite recent falling inflation
  • Both unemployment and household debt near record levels

By Brendan O'Boyle, Lais Morais and Marcela Ayres

From the butcher's shop where he works near Sao Paulo's historic center, Kleyton Zacarioto says customer traffic has been slowing for years thanks, he says, to a long period of rising food prices.

The prolonged squeeze on household budgets has turned the 39-year-old against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's bid for a fourth term in next month's election. Zacarioto says Lula is the only candidate he knows he will not vote for, though he recognized the president "did good things" when he was first in office in the 2000s.

“Someone who earns a minimum wage has no way to get ahead,” he said.

The 80-year-old Lula is asking voters for patience, while touting record low unemployment, falling inequality, and recent months of easing inflation to argue the economy is better than it seems.

But Zacarioto's frustration reflects a challenge that has dogged incumbents around the world since the pandemic: persuading voters that improving economic indicators matter when many still feel squeezed by years of higher prices.

"I know it's still not great, but I guarantee inflation will stay under control," Lula promised in a recent campaign spot, saying he knew what it was like to not make end's meet.

For months, polls have shown a neck-and-neck race between Lula and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro, who was barred from the race after being convicted of an attempted coup.

Polls suggest the economy is one of the main reasons Lula has struggled to fend off Senator Bolsonaro.

Nearly half of Brazilians say the economy has gotten worse in the past year, according to a Quaest poll published in September, compared to just 19% who say the economy improved.

Senator Bolsonaro has made concerns that paychecks do not stretch as far as they once did a centerpiece of his campaign, frequently contrasting current supermarket prices with those during his father's presidency.

Lula's campaign has pushed back with a website dubbed "Market of Lies" to dispute the claims. It has also filed a complaint in the Superior Electoral Court, which oversees elections in Brazil, accusing the senator's campaign of lying about prices.

THE 'VIBECESSION' HITS BRAZIL

Experts say the debate over the cost of living reflects a gap between improving labor and inflation measures and what many households experience day to day.

"All the big figures say that this has been a good government," said Thomas Traumann, a political analyst and author. "The fact is that everyday folks just don't agree with that."

Traumann drew comparisons to US President Joe Biden's struggles in 2024 to bridge a disconnect among voters between positive macroeconomic data and negative consumer sentiment, a moment economics commentator Kyla Scanlon dubbed the "vibecession."

"The government has achievements it can point to, but voters are asking how much of those gains have made it into their own households," said Felipe Nunes, founder and CEO of the pollster Quaest. "Voters judge the economy by their ability to pay bills, consume goods and services, and achieve their personal goals."

Food prices and rising debt burdens help explain why many families have seen little improvement in their post-pandemic spending power.

While food inflation has slowed sharply — and prices even fell in June to August — years of steep price increases continue to strain household budgets, with prices remaining well above pre-pandemic levels.

At the same time, household debt service excluding mortgages reached a record 26.6% of income in June, according to central bank data, as fast-growing fintechs offered easy credit at steep interest rates and a boom in online betting absorbed billions of reais of household income, pushing many families into financial distress.

The burden has been exacerbated by Brazil's 13.75% benchmark interest rate, one of the highest real rates in the world, which the central bank has gradually started to lower while keeping a close eye on inflation.

"If you look at labor-market data, poverty indicators and the expansion of the middle class, you see a picture of significant progress in recent years," said Marcelo Neri, an economist at Fundacao Getulio Vargas. "But when you factor in cumulative food inflation, interest rates and online betting, the result is, let's say, a draw with a lot of goals scored on both sides."

SKEPTICAL VOTERS

Lula has tried to react.

With two weeks to go before the first round, Lula rolled out measures that seemed aimed at boosting disposable income, including a 15% increase in a landmark welfare program, which will take effect before the second round of the elections in late October. He also announced an executive order banning online betting from October 6.

But polls suggest the measures have yet to make a meaningful impact on voter sentiment.

Back at the market, Carlos Alves da Silva has spent 15 years at the Barraca do Juca produce stand, its walls papered with posters showing the 1990s soap opera filmed there. He says it will not survive to 2028 if Lula wins.

"It's just a matter of taking on debt and scrambling to pay it off the following month," said Alves, who supports Senator Bolsonaro.

Candidates have tried to show a path forward.

Senator Bolsonaro is campaigning on lower food costs through tax cuts, better transport links, expanded grain storage and higher domestic fertilizer production. Lula points to growing farm output, government food stocks, and expanded rural credit.

But those proposals have yet to resonate with many Brazilians.

Conceicao Melquiades, visiting the market from Manaus, who is struggling to keep up with rising electricity and grocery prices, said she hasn’t seen any “real proposals” from the candidates.

"In the end not much is going to change."

data.title: Ethena: USDe token incentive program ends on a go-forward basis - Sep 2026
data.description:
Ethena is ending all token incentives and inflation tied to USDe on a go-forward basis, concluding the incentive program that had already declined roughly 85% since 2024. The change removes the last source of ENA dilution connected to the product's growth program.

With the program concluded, ENA no longer carries dilution from USDe growth incentives, giving holders a cleaner non-inflationary case for the token. Because emissions had already fallen about 85% from 2024, the incremental reduction in potential sell pressure is modest, so the change formalizes an existing trend rather than creating a new supply shock.

The practical effect is a simpler tokenomics profile: future ENA issuance is no longer tied to subsidizing USDe adoption, making supply dynamics easier to evaluate.

Ethena
@ethena

Since the initial airdrop in 2024 token incentives related to USDe growth have declined by roughly ~85% from 2024 to this year.

As of the end of this month there will be zero token incentives and inflation on a go forward basis related to USDe.

For all of those who participated…

data.title: Left for dead in the Amazon era, Toys "R" Us is growing again
data.description:
Toys "R" Us is making a strong brick-and-mortar move into the holiday season with a plan to open 120 new standalone stores in the U.S. The rollout will bring the toy chain's standalone footprint to 160 stores, up from about 40 existing locations. Toys "R" Us also operates branded shops inside Macy's stores.

The expansion is being executed with Go! Retail Group, which is a specialist in seasonal and experiential retail formats. The store expansion builds on the prior strategy of Toys "R" Us of staying relevant with 24 holiday pop-ups and airport activations over the last few years. The permanence and exact format of each site have not been fully detailed.

The initiative is also a strong step in Toys "R" Us rebuilding its U.S. presence after the 2017 bankruptcy and nationwide store closures. The Toys "R" Us bankruptcy wasn’t simply "Death by Amazon," as the company's biggest problem was roughly $5B in debt, much of it from a 2005 leveraged buyout. Heavy interest payments left less money to improve stores and online shopping while Amazon , Walmart , and Target competed for toy sales. As the company struggled, suppliers became wary, and some demanded payment upfront, making it harder to stock up for the crucial holiday season. Toys “R” Us filed for bankruptcy in 2017 hoping to reorganize, but disappointing holiday sales helped push its U.S. stores into liquidation in 2018. Since then, the brand has had a limited retail presence.

Toys "R" Us is currently owned by WHP Global, a New York-based brand management and licensing firm that acquired the brand in 2021. WHP also manages Babies R Us and other consumer brands.

A resurgence of Toys "R" Us stores is of interest to retailers and e-commerce companies, including Walmart , Target , Amazon , and Costco . Specialty sellers such as GameStop , as well as online toy marketplaces and direct-to-consumer collectible brands, could also be impacted. The added Toys “R” Us locations could also boost overall holiday toy inventory, which would be a positive for Mattel and Hasbro .

data.title: The 10-Point: Moving Everything Americans Buy Is Getting More Expensive — WSJ Newsletter
data.description:
Emma Tucker

1. FROM MY DESK

It is getting more expensive to move pretty much everything Americans buy. Trucking and cargo-shipping rates have climbed to their highest levels since the supply-chain disruptions of the Covid era by some key measures, adding another source of inflationary pressure across the economy.

Record diesel prices are a major reason, but they aren't the only one. Our reporters examine the rising transportation costs crimping margins at companies and likely to bleed into everything from clothing to food.

Rising fuel costs are adding to the squeeze at the buffet line, too. Cash-strapped consumers are clamoring for endless amounts of chips, fries or shrimp, and restaurants like Golden Corral are trying to capitalize with all-you-can-eat offerings. But mounting costs are making those bottomless deals harder to pull off. Heather Haddon shows how America's biggest buffet chain is making the tricky math of unlimited meals work.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES

  • President Trump has rejected Iran's proposal for a seven-day ceasefire and told aides he expects to resume bombing after the midterm elections. The president is predicting midterm success even as Republicans grow increasingly worried about his falling approval ratings.
  • Trump's warm reception for China's Xi Jinping drew bipartisan criticism, but early this morning the countries said they had agreed to lower tariffs on $30 billion of less sensitive trade in either direction.
  • A top U.S. Treasury Department official hopscotched across the Middle East and Europe this month with a warning to Iran's trading partners: You either trade with Tehran or Washington.
  • Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, a frequent target for Trump and Republicans, says in an interview that it isn't in her nature to back down.
  • For the third time this month, the Supreme Court brushed aside a last-gasp bid by the state GOP to install a gerrymandered congressional map for the midterms.
  • Dozens of U.S. military personnel joined Ecuadorean police in raids against drug traffickers.

3. FROM THE MARKETS

  • U.S. stocks ended the week higher, with the Dow snapping a three-session losing streak as investors looked past rising Treasury yields, volatile oil prices and uncertainty over the Middle East conflict.
  • A Pentagon-backed oil company is racing to boost production in Venezuela and could soon challenge Chevron's longstanding position as the country's largest private oil producer.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

The mystery man shadowing Kimberly Guilfoyle as she pushes energy deals across Europe.

Guilfoyle is parlaying her ambassadorship to Greece into one of the Trump administration's most important diplomatic roles. In the nearly 11 months since she arrived in Athens, the former prosecutor and Fox News host has crisscrossed the Balkans to promote a "vertical gas corridor" to receive American natural gas in Greece and funnel it toward Ukraine. But she has puzzled officials across the region with her persistent promotion of a Greek construction firm called Aktor Group and the extensive efforts she has taken to involve Christos Marafatsos, chairman of Greek Voices for Trump. Marafatsos has attended so many of her meetings that some foreign officials mistook him for her chief of staff. In fact, he is a top lobbyist for Aktor, report Rebecca Ballhaus, Dana Mattioli, Joe Parkinson and Drew Hinshaw.

5.

Overwhelmed by Ukrainian drone attacks, Russia is making businesses defend themselves.

Companies across the country are leasing air-defense systems, building their own and even hiring gunners to shoot down drones as strikes intensify deep inside Russian territory. It isn't all by choice: The Kremlin has warned that companies that don't take responsibility for their protection against Ukrainian drones could face temporary state seizure. The threat is even changing job requirements: Some companies are looking for security guards who can patrol sites, watch the skies, spot drones and shoot them down. Thomas Grove and Daria Matviichuk report on how Russia is making drone defense everyone's problem.

Enjoy the best of the Journal's feature writing. Get a weekly look at our most colorful, thought-provoking and original features on the business of life. Sign up for the WSJ Weekend Reads newsletter.

6. SEE THE STORY

How Asheville's artists and shopkeepers rebuilt their city.

Two years after Hurricane Helene brought 25-foot floods to Buncombe County in North Carolina, artists and business owners are reopening, relocating and starting over, often with their own savings. One couple poured more than $900,000 from savings and loans into repairing a historic warehouse, while a damaged building became an outdoor skating rink and an artist who lost more than 50 works converted his garage into a new studio. See how Asheville's community is rebuilding after the storm.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

  • Saturday: No. 1 Texas takes on No. 14 Tennessee in a major college-football matchup in Knoxville, with Trump expected to attend.
  • Sunday: MTV presents its Video Music Awards. MLB's regular season wraps up.
  • Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER

$261,810

That's the starting price of the Ferrari Amalfi in the U.S. It's the Italian automaker's least expensive car, but after taking it for a test drive, our auto columnist Dan Neil argues it's the Ferrari worth having, favoring its relatively understated looks and twin-turbo performance over the more expensive models. Of course, "least expensive" is relative: His test car had another $143,710 worth of personalization.

9. AND FINALLY...

For some newlyweds, the perfect wedding gift is a little help toward a first home.

Nearly seven out of eight couples plan to add a cash fund of some kind to their wedding registries, and almost 40% of recipients are putting the money toward buying a home or moving to a new one. As the cost of buying a home has soared, couples are more comfortable asking for cash alongside-or instead of-traditional gifts. Some are even displaying QR codes for home funds at their wedding celebrations.

10. BEYOND THE NEWSROOM

  • Opinion: A political body like Congress is hardly an ideal referee for college sports, but a Senate bill may be the only way to stop states from exploiting the Supreme Court's 2021 NCAA ruling.
  • WSJ | Buy Side: Zip into cozy, layerable quarter-zips with these stylist-approved sweaters.

ABOUT US

The 10-Point is your guide to The Wall Street Journal's reporting and analysis you can't get anywhere else. Your subscription makes our journalism possible.

data.title: Adroit Industries, ArMee Infotech, Swastika Infra, Elevate Campuses: Check GMP, full subscription ahead of allotment
data.description:
IPO GMP Today, Sept. 26 -- Four IPOs - Adroit Industries, ArMee Infotech, Swastika Infra and Elevate Campuses - have concluded their three-day subscription windows, shifting the focus to the allotment process and their expected stock market debut. The allotment status for all four public issues is likely to be finalised on Monday, September 28.

The four IPOs were open for subscription from September 23 to September 25. With bidding now closed, investors are awaiting details on share allotment while also tracking the latest grey market premium (GMP) for the issues ahead of their proposed listings.

Successful bidders are expected to receive the shares in their demat accounts on September 29. The four companies are scheduled to list their shares on the NSE and BSE on September 30, 2026, subject to the tentative listing schedule.

Here's a detailed look at the latest GMP, subscription numbers, IPO allotment timeline and other key details of Adroit Industries, ArMee Infotech, Swastika Infra and Elevate Campuses.

Adroit Industries has emerged as the strongest grey market performer among the four issues, with grey market premium (GMP) stood at Rs.48. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band and the prevailing GMP, the estimated listing price works out to Rs.182 per share, indicating a premium of 35.82%.

The IPO received an overall subscription of around 176.85 times during the three-day bidding period. The retail portion was subscribed 99.81 times, while the non-institutional investor (NII) category was subscribed 332.35 times. The qualified institutional buyer (QIB) segment received bids for 195.04 times the shares on offer.

Investors can check their Adroit Industries IPO allotment status through the BSE, NSE or the registrar's website, Bigshare Services - https://www.bigshareonline.com/ipo_Allotment.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com

To check the allotment status, investors need to first select 'Equity' and then choose the issue name from the dropdown menu. They can enter their application number or PAN, selecting the 'Permanent Account Number' option if they wish to check using their PAN. Investors then need to complete the 'I am not a robot' verification and click on 'Search'. The share application status will subsequently be displayed on the screen.

The Rs.150.71 crore Adroit Industries IPO comprised a fresh issue of 98.97 lakh shares aggregating to Rs.132.62 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 13.50 lakh shares worth Rs.18.09 crore. The company had set the final issue price at Rs.134 per share. Incorporated in January 1995, Adroit Industries (India) is a vertically integrated manufacturer and supplier of propeller shafts and torque-transmission components used in driveline systems.

ArMee Infotech shares are commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs.8 ahead of their stock market debut. Based on the upper end of the IPO price band, the implied listing price stands at Rs.383 per share, representing a 2.13% premium over the issue price of Rs.375.

The Rs.300 crore IPO received a total subscription of 2.6 times during the three-day bidding period. Among investor categories, the QIB portion was subscribed 3.2 times, while the retail segment received 2.65 times subscription. The NII portion was subscribed 2.24 times.

Investors can access their ArMee Infotech IPO allotment details through the BSE, NSE or Cameo Corporate Services, the registrar handling the issue - https://ipo.cameoindia.com/

On the relevant allotment page, investors need to choose the equity segment and select ArMee Infotech from the list of issues. They can check their application status using either their application number or PAN. Those using PAN will need to select the appropriate option, enter the required details, complete the captcha and submit the request.

The public issue comprised 80 lakh fresh equity shares, with the company raising the entire Rs.300 crore through the fresh issue. ArMee Infotech had set the IPO price band at Rs.350-375 per share. Founded in 2003 and based in Ahmedabad, ArMee Infotech operates in the IT sector, offering IT infrastructure solutions and managed services.

Swastika Infra shares are commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs.4.5. At the upper end of the IPO price band, the current GMP indicates an estimated listing price of Rs.189.5 per share, implying a 2.43% premium over the issue price of Rs.185.

The public issue attracted strong demand across investor categories, with the IPO receiving 7.91 times overall subscription. The NII portion was subscribed 19.35 times, while the retail category received 5.64 times subscription. The QIB segment was subscribed 3.31 times.

Investors can check the Swastika Infra IPO allotment status through the BSE, NSE or MUFG Intime, the registrar to the issue. - https://in.mpms.mufg.com/Initial_Offer/public-issues.html

To view the allotment details, investors need to select the 'Equity' category and choose Swastika Infra from the issue name dropdown. They can then check the status using either their application number or PAN. For a PAN-based search, investors need to select the 'Permanent Account Number' option, enter the relevant details, complete the 'I am not a robot' verification and click on 'Search'. The application status will then be displayed on the screen.

The Swastika Infra IPO is a Rs.160.88 crore book-built issue, comprising both a fresh issue and an offer for sale. The fresh issue consists of 69.46 lakh shares worth Rs.128.50 crore, while the OFS comprises 17.50 lakh shares aggregating to Rs.32.38 crore. The company had fixed the IPO price band at Rs.175 to Rs.185 per share, with Rs.185 being the upper end of the price range.

Incorporated in August 2019, Swastika Infra Limited is an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) company specializing in power transmission and distribution (T&D) infrastructure projects.

Elevate Campuses shares are currently commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs.4. At the top end of the IPO price band, this translates into an estimated listing price of Rs.366 per share, implying a 1.1% premium over the issue price of Rs.362.

The public issue received 1.89 times overall subscription, with demand varying across investor categories. The QIB portion was subscribed 2.66 times, while the retail segment received 1.07 times subscription. The NII category was subscribed 0.89 times.

Investors can access their Elevate Campuses IPO allotment status through the BSE, NSE or KFin Technologies, the registrar to the issue. - https://ipostatus.kfintech.com/

To check the allotment result, investors first need to choose the 'Equity' category and select Elevate Campuses from the issue-name dropdown. The status can then be retrieved using either the application number or PAN. Investors opting for a PAN-based search should select the 'Permanent Account Number' option, enter their details, complete the 'I am not a robot' verification and click 'Search'. The application status will then be displayed.

The Elevate Campuses IPO is a Rs.2,100 crore book-built issue, consisting entirely of a fresh issue. The company is issuing 5.80 crore shares, aggregating to Rs.2,100 crore. The IPO price band was fixed at Rs.343 to Rs.362 per share, with Rs.362 being the upper end of the price range.

Incorporated in 2005, Elevate Campuses Ltd. is an education infrastructure company engaged in owning, operating and managing on-campus student accommodation for higher education institutions (HEIs) and owning K-12 school assets.

data.title: Azerbaijan signs investment agreements worth more than $10 billion
data.description:
Azerbaijan signed agreements representing more than $10 billion in potential investment at an international forum in Baku, a presidential aide said on Saturday, as the country also announced a series of energy deals.

State oil company SOCAR, France's TotalEnergies and Abu Dhabi's XRG reached a final investment decision on the full-field development of the Absheron gas and condensate field.

President Ilham Aliyev said the second phase of Absheron, one of the largest offshore fields in the Caspian Sea, would increase Azerbaijan's gas production by around 5 billion cubic metres within three to four years.

"Oil and gas will continue to dominate our economy and to generate wealth which will be reinvested," Aliyev told the Azerbaijan International Investment Forum. He said the non-oil sector now accounted for more than 70% of GDP, while oil and gas still made up more than 90% of exports.

Azerbaijan exports gas mainly to Europe and Turkey, with about half of its 25 billion cubic metres of exports last year going to EU countries. The expansion comes as disruptions to global energy supplies have heightened concerns over security of supply, although further growth in Azerbaijani exports to Europe would require additional pipeline capacity.

SOCAR and US energy major ExxonMobil signed a production-sharing agreement for the exploration, development and production of unconventional hydrocarbon resources in Azerbaijan's Middle Kura basin, with each company holding a 50% stake and ExxonMobil serving as operator.

Aliyev also said transit cargo volumes through the country are expected to reach 16 million metric tons this year, with a target of 25 million tons or more by 2030, while the government was negotiating with international companies, which it did not name, to develop data centres and AI in Azerbaijan.

data.title: NTPC, EDF Power form joint venture to develop low-carbon energy projects | Details here
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 26 -- State-run power utility National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) Limited and EDF Power Solutions India Private Limited, a wholly owned arm of the French power firm EDF, entered into a 50:50 joint venture to build and operate low-carbon energy infrastructure.

According to a release, the agreement focuses on the development, ownership, and operation of pumped storage assets, hydroelectric installations, other renewable energy facilities, and electricity distribution operations.

The newly created entity holds a mandate to execute power projects within domestic borders and across neighbouring nations.

The pact was formally executed on September 25 in the presence of Gurdeep Singh, Chairman and Managing Director of NTPC Limited, and Bernard Fontana, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of EDF SA, France.

Under the terms detailed in the release, the corporate partnership aims to build a joint industrial enterprise dedicated to green transition assets. The official statement highlighted that both firms remain committed to establishing a responsible and innovative industrial company.

"Through this strategic partnership, NTPC and EDF Power Solutions are committed to establish a responsible and innovative industrial company to develop, build and operate low carbon powerplants as well as flexibility solutions and transmission assets," the release said.

The strategic partnership aligns its project pipeline with the nation's long-term energy transition targets, specifically supporting the government target of reaching 100 gigawatts of installed pumped storage capacity by the year 2036.

The companies confirmed that they intend to combine their technical and operational resources, stating that the entities will work "to provide tailormade offers, drive the decarbonization and global performance of electrical systems."

The release noted that both power operators expect their collaborative resources to supply regular renewable capacity additions, stating that both firms stand prepared "to contribute significantly to India's renewable energy market, driving innovation and fostering environmental stewardship."

data.title: Senior citizen wrongly paid tax on tax-free bonds: What the Rs.9.91 lakh ITAT case means
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 26 -- An error in tax filing resulted in a senior citizen paying Rs.9.91 lakh in tax on interest from tax-free bonds. The individual has now secured relief from the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT). The tribunal, after reviewing the basic facts of the case, has directed the concerned tax authorities to grant relief by issuing a refund along with applicable interest. The final order in this case was pronounced on 23 September 2026.

This is a very important case for taxpayers, as it offers several fundamental and vital lessons for day-to-day tax filing. This is because, in this case, the tribunal primarily distinguished between making a fresh tax-related claim and rectifying an error already apparent from the income tax return initially filed.

In this case, Ajay Kumar Bakaya, a senior citizen and resident of Gurugram, invested Rs.3 crore in tax-free bonds in February 2013. Out of this, Rs.2 crore was invested in India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL) bonds. These bonds carried an interest rate of 8.48%. Whereas Rs.1 crore was invested in Rural Electrification Corporation (REC) bonds carrying 8.46% interest.

As per the Income Tax Act, 1961, the interest from these bonds was exempt under Section 10(15)(iv)(h). Bakaya had reported the interest earned from these investments as 'exempt income' in his return for the assessment years (AYs) 2018-19 to 2024-25.

Still, while filing his return for AY 2022-23, he erroneously reported Rs.25.42 lakh of bond interest as taxable income under 'income from other sources'. This consisted of Rs.16.96 lakh from IIFCL and Rs.8.46 lakh from REC. The mistake resulted in an excess, i.e., additional tax of Rs.9,91,370.

Furthermore, by the time Bakaya discovered the error, the deadline for filing a revised return under Section 139(5) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, had expired. On 19 January 2024, he approached the assessing officer (AO) under Section 154 to seek assistance with rectification and a refund.

The AO rejected the request in an order dated 7 April 2025, relying on the Supreme Court's decision in Goetze (India) Ltd. v. CIT. The AO stated that the claim can not be entertained without a revised return through appropriate channels.

The matter eventually reached the ITAT after the CIT(A) upheld the position. The tribunal clearly noted that Bakaya was not requesting for a new exemption claim. The interest income was already declared in the return without concealment of material facts. The error was that an otherwise exempt receipt had been classified as 'taxable income'.

The ITAT hence held that a rectification was nothing but a correction of a 'mistake apparent from the record' and not a fresh claim. It was also held that the ruling Goetze (India) Ltd. was not applicable to the facts and circumstances of this case.

The tribunal relied on the decision taken in the case law of Kapil Dev Nikhanj v. ACIT, which elucidated that tax must be collected in accordance with the law of the land. The collection should not be arbitrary. The tribunal consequently instructed AO to treat the bond interest as exempt under Section 10(15)(iv)(h) and grant a subsequent refund of Rs.9,91,370 along with the applicable interest as admissible under law.

In summary, the broader lesson is straightforward: paying tax on legally exempt income does not necessarily resolve the matter if the mistake is later discovered. Still, taxpayers should not wait for a dispute to arise.

It is prudent to be vigilant and exercise caution when reviewing exempt income, deductions, and tax classifications before filing. Such an approach can help prevent excess tax payments and the need for time-consuming rectification proceedings.

data.title: On HR Professionals Day, CHROs Ask: Who Supports The Supporters?
data.description:
Layoffs, return-to-office battles and AI-led change have piled onto HR’s plate, prompting four CHROs to call for stronger support systems for the people managing them

Every HR Professionals Day, the conversation circles back to what HR does for everyone else — onboarding, layoffs, culture, employee wellbeing and the difficult conversations that come with organisational change. Far less often is the question asked: who does this for HR itself?

The question is becoming harder to ignore as the demands placed on HR continue to expand. A global study by SHRM found that HR professionals’ confidence in their organisation’s mental health support fell from 70 per cent in 2024 to 65 per cent in 2025. Meanwhile, a Deloitte study on workplace mental health found that more than half of employees surveyed across Indian industries reported emotional exhaustion and burnout — challenges HR teams are expected to identify and address, even as their own pressures receive less attention.

For HR leaders, the challenge is not simply managing a larger workload. It is the emotional and organisational responsibility of helping employees navigate uncertainty while often experiencing that uncertainty themselves.

The Load Has Intensified

For Megha Goel, Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), Godrej Properties, the shift is less about entirely new problems and more about existing challenges arriving simultaneously, leaving little room to process one before the next begins."A high emotional quotient is no longer a nice to have for HR, it is treated as the baseline, with fairness, objectivity and empathy sitting at the heart of it," said Goel.

Layoffs in one part of a business while keeping the wider workforce engaged, return-to-office conversations that touch personal circumstances, and AI-led changes that raise questions about employees’ relevance have created what Goel describes as "a very different kind of labour, repeated across audiences, day after day."

The pressure also comes from HR’s role in shaping organisational culture. While culture is intended to be a shared leadership responsibility, HR often designs and facilitates it and is held accountable when it falters. The question of who supports the people carrying that responsibility, however, is less frequently addressed.

Leading Change Alone

Sonal Jain, Global Chief Human Resource and Transformation Officer, EPL, sees the challenge as structural rather than simply emotional. HR frequently finds itself at the centre of the same organisational changes it is expected to help employees navigate."I believe organisations need to build an ecosystem where people across functions are able to look after each other, with support systems, processes and people they can look up to," said Jain.

One additional challenge is confidentiality. HR professionals routinely handle sensitive information that cannot be discussed with colleagues or peers, making formal and confidential support mechanisms particularly important.

Jain pointed to mechanisms such as Employee Assistance Programmes and confidential feedback channels as potential avenues for HR professionals to seek support without compromising the confidentiality inherent to their roles.

For Pooja Singh, CHRO, PSPL Group, the isolation can also stem from how HR is perceived within an organisation. The function’s proximity to performance management, workplace concerns and organisational decisions can make its presence feel evaluative, making it harder to build the informal relationships that often help employees manage workplace pressure."A sustainable HR function is not one that simply absorbs pressure," said Singh. "It is one that has the authority, resources, support and organisational trust to manage complexity effectively."

Beyond Wellness Programmes

The four CHROs converge on a broader point: wellness programmes alone cannot address the pressures facing HR.For Goel, organisational credibility is central. When HR is trusted to lead through functional expertise and business context, it has greater room to handle difficult situations effectively. Leadership support is equally important, particularly when HR has to communicate or implement unpopular decisions.

Singh argues that responsibility for employee wellbeing and organisational culture cannot rest with HR alone."Managers and business leaders must share accountability for employee well-being, workplace culture and successful change," she said. "HR can provide the framework, expertise and leadership, but it cannot be the organisation's sole emotional and cultural shock absorber."

Jain believes HR also needs a stronger voice in decisions it is subsequently expected to execute, particularly when leaders are dealing with difficult organisational choices. She argues that this voice should be supported by data and analytics rather than instinct alone."Culture is built piece by piece, and if one part of that foundation is removed, the whole structure can be affected," she said.

For Shikha Gupta, CHRO, Luminous Power Technologies, one of the most practical gaps lies in how HR uses the wellbeing resources it makes available to others."It is important that we proactively leverage them for our own wellbeing and resilience," said Gupta.

Boundaries As A Skill

For Gupta, one of the most important lessons in sustaining an HR leadership role is understanding the relationship between empathy and boundaries."Empathy is most effective when paired with healthy boundaries," she said. "Sustaining yourself is not separate from being an effective leader; it is an essential part of it."

Singh similarly distinguishes resilience from simply absorbing organisational pressure. For HR professionals, resilience cannot mean carrying the weight of difficult decisions and employee concerns in isolation.

That distinction is increasingly relevant as the function’s remit expands. HR leaders are expected to support employees through restructuring, changing work models, technology-led transformation and evolving expectations around wellbeing, while also advising business leaders and protecting organisational culture.

Building Support For HR

Across the four conversations, the common thread is not a call for HR to step away from its responsibilities, but for organisations to recognise that the function itself needs an ecosystem of support.

That could mean greater leadership accountability for employee wellbeing, confidential support mechanisms for HR professionals, stronger peer networks, clearer boundaries and greater organisational backing when HR teams make difficult decisions.

For a function tasked with building resilient workplaces, the question is therefore increasingly reciprocal: what structures are organisations creating to ensure that the people supporting everyone else have the support, authority and space to sustain themselves?As Singh puts it, if HR’s job is to build resilient organisations, “it is equally important that HR is resilient enough to take the lead.”

data.title: Mahajan Takes Charge As Chief Financial & Growth Officer At Lotus Singapore Group
data.description:
Gaurav mahajan brings 17 years of experience across finance, strategy, investments and commercial operations to the new role

Gaurav Mahajan has been appointed Chief Financial and Growth Officer at Lotus Singapore Group, taking responsibility for investments, capital allocation, growth initiatives and long-term value creation across its markets. He joins the organisation with more than 17 years of experience spanning corporate finance, strategy, investments, commercial operations and business leadership.

Broad Finance Experience

Mahajan is a Chartered Accountant and holds an MBA in Finance and Strategy from the Indian School of Business. His career has included roles across corporate environments, startups, venture capital and consulting.

Before joining Lotus Singapore Group, Mahajan spent more than four years with Adani Enterprises, where he held responsibilities across the Group CEO Office of Adani Natural Resources and contract administration for mining operations.

His work at Adani involved strategy, business reviews, performance improvement and coordination across operational, commercial, technical and legal functions.

Strategy And Operations

Earlier, Mahajan was Head of Business Operations and Finance at Venture Highway, where he worked across finance and business operations.

He also spent four years with Carlsberg Group, holding roles in corporate development, strategy and projects. His responsibilities included strategic planning and corporate development initiatives.

Mahajan has also worked as an independent management consultant, handling projects related to supply chains, finance process restructuring, business planning and reporting.

New Growth Mandate

At Lotus Singapore Group, Mahajan's role will cover the development of its investment engine, capital allocation and portfolio growth across Singapore and India.

The position brings together his experience in financial management, corporate strategy and commercial operations, with a broader mandate spanning investment and growth.

Mahajan's appointment comes as he moves into a role combining finance leadership with business and investment responsibilities.

data.title: Radico Khaitan Refreshes 1965 Spirit Of Victory Lemon Dash Premium Rum
data.description:
The refreshed flavoured rum makes its debut in Assam, with a phased rollout planned across Odisha, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal

Radico Khaitan refreshes the identity of its Lemon Dash Flavoured Rum, marking the next phase in the evolution of its 1965 Spirit of Victory franchise. The new-look Lemon Dash debuts in Assam, with a phased rollout planned across key markets including Odisha, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.

The refresh builds on the 1965 Spirit of Victory franchise, which is a million-case brand in Radico Khaitan’s portfolio. Originally launched in 2017 as a tribute to the soldiers of the 1965 Indo-Pak war, the franchise first enters the market through the Canteen Stores Department (CSD) before expanding into the domestic market.

Lemon Dash launches in 2022 as the franchise’s entry into the premium flavoured rum segment, offering a citrus-led proposition. The refreshed identity combines the heritage of 1965 Spirit of Victory with the character of Gandharaj lemon.

Kunal Madan, Chief Marketing Officer, Radico Khaitan, says, “1965 Spirit of Victory has always stood for a distinctive combination of heritage, pride and character. With Lemon Dash, we wanted to bring that heritage into a fresher, more expressive space.”

The new packaging features a cream-and-gold palette with deep green accents, metallic detailing and illustrated Gandharaj lemons. A tall, textured glass bottle, embossed detailing and the brand’s signature roundel badge reinforce the premium positioning. The four pillars of Honour, Courage, Brotherhood and Glory continue to anchor the franchise’s heritage.

The product combines citrus-infused rum with Gandharaj lemon, offering a bright aroma, smooth texture and fresh finish. Lemon Dash also receives a Gold Quality Award at Monde Selection.

The refreshed Lemon Dash Flavoured Rum is currently available in Assam in three formats: a 750 ml glass bottle with mono carton, a 375 ml glass bottle and a 180 ml glass bottle. The new packaging rolls out in phases across other key Lemon Dash markets, including Odisha, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal.

Founded in 1943 as Rampur Distillery Company, Radico Khaitan is among India’s major manufacturers of Indian-made foreign liquor (IMFL). The company develops its own brands, including Rampur Indian Single Malt Whiskies, Jaisalmer Indian Craft Gin, Magic Moments Vodka, 1965 Spirit of Victory Premium XXX Rum and Lemon Dash Premium Flavoured Rum.

data.title: Muthoot Fincorp Bags BCCI Title Sponsorship Rights For Indian Cricket
data.description:
The financial services company holds the title sponsorship rights for India’s international and domestic home matches until March 31, 2028

Muthoot Fincorp emerges as the title sponsor for Indian cricket for the next two years, according to media reports.

The Kochi-based financial services company, part of the Muthoot Group, holds the title sponsorship rights for India’s international and domestic matches played at home until March 31, 2028.

The sponsorship forms part of the Board of Control for Cricket in India’s (BCCI) latest commercial cycle, which runs through March 2028. It follows recent title sponsorship associations with companies including Hero MotoCorp, SBI Life and ChatGPT.

The two-year arrangement covers around 35 home international matches, including 10 Tests, 12 One Day Internationals (ODIs) and 13 Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is). The schedule also coincides with India’s three-match ODI series against the West Indies.

India’s upcoming home season also features bilateral series involving Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe, along with matches against other international teams.

data.title: Adani Group Unit Gets Nod For Rs 1.04 Lakh Cr Data Centre Park In Odisha
data.description:
The Adani Group unit’s proposed investment is part of four data centre and AI projects approved with a combined value of about Rs 1.42 lakh crore

High Density Data Centre, a unit of the Adani Group, has received approval to invest Rs 1.04 lakh crore to develop a 1 GW data centre park in Odisha.

The project was cleared by the High-Level Clearance Authority chaired by Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi. The Odisha government has earmarked about 250 acres at Naraj for the facility.

The proposed investment comes as demand for data centre capacity increases with the adoption of artificial intelligence. The project is among the largest proposed investments in India’s data centre sector.

Four Projects Get Clearance

The Odisha government also approved three other data centre and artificial intelligence-related projects, with a combined investment of Rs 38,391 crore. Together, the four projects have a total proposed investment of about Rs 1.42 lakh crore.

HCLTech has received approval for a Rs 14,257 crore AI-optimised data centre in Khordha in partnership with Indian AI company Sarvam AI.

Sentraforge AI, a joint venture between Megha Engineering and Infrastructures and GVPR Engineers, plans to invest Rs 22,634 crore in a 120 MW sovereign AI campus and global capability centre in Puri.

RKD Construction has received clearance for a Rs 1,500 crore data centre in Cuttack district.

Data Centre Hub Planned Near Bhubaneswar

The state has identified a 140-acre site at Tangiapada near Bhubaneswar’s Info Valley for a data centre hub. The site will accommodate the HCLTech and Sentraforge projects.

The Adani Group’s data centre business, AdaniConneX, operates a facility in Chennai and is developing projects in Mumbai, Pune and Hyderabad.

The Rs 1.04 lakh crore Odisha project is slightly below the Rs 1.08 lakh crore data centre project announced by Reliance Industries in Andhra Pradesh, which includes an artificial intelligence data centre and a cable landing station.

The approvals come as Indian states seek to attract investments in data centres and AI infrastructure, supported by growing demand for computing capacity and related digital infrastructure.

data.title: PSU Banks Waive ATM Charges During Sept 28-30 Strike
data.description:
PSU bank ATM charges will be waived beyond free limits from September 28-30 as branches face disruption during the three-day bank strike

Public sector banks are waiving ATM withdrawal charges beyond the usual free transaction limits during the three-day bank strike from September 28 to 30, giving customers access to cash without additional ATM fees as branch operations face disruption. State Bank of India (SBI), Punjab National Bank (PNB), Bank of Baroda (BoB), Union Bank of India, Indian Bank and several other state-owned lenders have announced the waiver.

The move is aimed at reducing inconvenience to customers during the strike called by the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) over the demand for a five-day banking week. The strike follows a one-day nationwide action on September 11 and could result in an extended disruption because September 26 and 27 fall on Saturday and Sunday.

ATM Charges Waived Beyond Free Limits

Under the existing RBI framework, savings-account customers generally receive five free monthly transactions at their own bank’s ATMs. At other-bank ATMs, the free limit is three transactions in six metropolitan cities and five in non-metro locations.

After the applicable free limit is exhausted, banks can levy a charge of up to Rs 23 per transaction, excluding GST. During September 28-30, participating PSU banks will waive these charges, allowing customers to make additional ATM withdrawals without the normal fee. SBI has separately confirmed that ATM transaction charges will be waived during the strike period and has advised customers to use ATMs and digital banking channels for essential services.

UPI, Digital Banking To Remain Available

Customers will continue to have access to UPI, mobile banking and internet banking for routine transactions. NEFT, RTGS and IMPS can also be used through digital channels supported by individual banks. PSU banks have advised customers to complete transactions requiring branch-level assistance before the strike. Public sector and regional rural banks will also open on Sunday, September 27, giving customers an additional opportunity to complete physical banking work before the strike begins.

The strike is scheduled for September 28, 29 and 30, with five-day banking remaining the principal unresolved demand. The unions have also announced an indefinite strike from October 26 if their demands remain unresolved. The ATM fee waiver is therefore expected to provide some relief for customers who need cash during the strike, while digital payment channels will remain the primary alternative for routine banking requirements.

data.title: DHL Express To Raise India Shipping Rates 8.9% From 2027
data.description:
Annual price revision from January 1 comes amid higher inflation, currency volatility and operating costs

DHL Express will increase its shipment charges in India by 8.9 per cent from January 1, 2027, as part of its annual price revision, with the logistics company citing inflation, currency movements and higher costs across its operations.

The increase will apply to DHL Express shipments originating from India and comes as logistics companies face higher operating expenses, including energy, labour, compliance and administrative costs.

Annual Price Revision

DHL Express reviews its pricing annually to reflect changes in operating conditions. The company has previously said that its adjustments take into account inflation, currency dynamics and administrative costs associated with evolving regulatory, customs and security requirements.

For businesses using international express delivery, the higher rates are likely to add to logistics costs, particularly for companies engaged in cross-border ecommerce, manufacturing and international trade.

The company operates across more than 220 countries and territories, making its cost base sensitive to developments across multiple markets and currencies.

Currency Volatility Adds To Cost Pressure

The latest rate revision follows DHL Express India's introduction of a Currency Effects Index (CFX) for Time Definite International shipments from August 1, 2026. The formula-based mechanism is designed to address significant increases in operating costs arising from currency volatility and foreign exchange movements.

DHL Express India has said the company typically factors a 2-3 per cent annual depreciation of the rupee against the US dollar or euro into its pricing, while larger movements can create additional cost pressures.

Continued Investment In Network And Technology

Despite the higher charges, DHL Express continues to invest in its India operations. The company has a €1 billion investment programme in India covering 2025-30, including infrastructure, technology, service centres, airside facilities and fleet expansion.

The company has also been expanding its use of automation and artificial intelligence across operations and customer touchpoints, while focusing on network optimisation to manage costs and improve efficiency.

The latest increase means Indian businesses and consumers using DHL Express will face higher shipping costs from the beginning of 2027, with the actual amount payable depending on the service and shipment characteristics.

data.title: The ‘Economic Singularity’ Could Fuel Crypto’s Next Supercycle, Says Raoul Pal
data.description:
Key points:
  • Raoul Pal said on Friday crypto’s recent drawdown was a "mid-cycle fall," not the end of a full cycle.
  • He said a leverage flush still has to come before the market can really move higher.
  • He said the "economic singularity" arrives around 2030, when AI agents become a productive population.

Global Macro Investor founder Raoul Pal said on Friday that crypto's drawdown was a "mid-cycle fall and not a full cycle," and that the market's biggest move would come later this decade, when AI agents push the economy into an "economic singularity" around 2030.

In an interview on the Crypto Insider podcast, Pal explained that the current setup resembled 2019 and 2020, when Bitcoin traded flat for months before the rally that took it to record highs in 2021, trading above $65,000 in November of the year.

He said the four-year cycle fooled people. Traders waited for one last dip that did not come, and the buying since has come from those who missed it. He added one caution, however. A quick leverage flush still has to happen before the market can really get going, according to Pal.

Why Bitcoin Lagged?

Liquidity is driving both, not the headlines or the earnings, according to macro investor Raoul Pal. “Bitcoin is 87% correlated with global liquidity; the Nasdaq is 97% correlated.” That gap explains part of the split this year. The Nasdaq Composite (IXIC) has gained 16.46% year-to-date. Bitcoin fell almost 4% over the same period. Liquidity makes Bitcoin swing harder, said Pal, because it’s young, volatile and emotional. “It is running cold," he said.

The token peaked above $126,000 in October last year, and has spent 2026 well below that level, trading flat, before reaching an eight-month high last week.

Liquidity grew in the US but not by much, he said. Measured against gross domestic product (GDP) growth, excess liquidity was barely positive and often slightly negative. That left enough capital to fund one trade, and that trade was AI. "AI has paused, and crypto's gone," Pal said. He described the move as a rotation rather than fresh money entering the market.

Liquidity Runs Past 2027

The debt cycle would normally put liquidity into the first half of 2027 before stalling, Pal said. He thinks it will run longer this time. Two things will extend it, according to Pal. The government has been issuing its debt at the short end of the curve, and the AI capex supercycle needs funding of its own. That gives the market two sources of liquidity rather than one. He said traders should watch the dollar above all.

A weaker dollar was the signal, he said, and that is when crypto and gold tend to move.

The Singularity Trade

Beyond the liquidity cycle, Pal said the growth engine changed. He called AI and robots "digital immigrants," a new population joining the “workforce as infinite numbers.” That lifted productivity and let GDP growth outpace debt growth, which was how the debt problem would be resolved. Pal put that turnaround by 2030, calling it the "economic singularity,” and said that GDP growth could reach 20% to 30% in the early 2030s.

Pal said the shift was already visible in company numbers. He said the technology companies stopped hiring three years ago, and that revenue per employee at Meta (META) has since doubled. At Nvidia (NVDA), he said the figure went from $2 million to $10 million per employee, and Amazon (AMZN) began investing in robotics in 2019 and will have more robots than humans working for it by next year.

Crypto, however, was the rail, according to Pal. He said AI agents needed a coordination layer for value and identity, and that blockchains were well suited to it. He said he held Ethereum (ETH), Solana (SOL), and Sui (SUI) for that reason.

Bitcoin’s price was down by 0.5% over the past 24 hours, while the apex cryptocurrency fell from the $ 85,000 range. On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bullish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘normal’ levels over the past day.

data.title: US, China Agree To A $30B Reciprocal Tariff Cut Deal And Launch A Dialogue On AI As Xi Reiterates Two Countries Can Overcome ‘Thucydides Trap’
data.description:
Key points:
  • The two countries also endorsed the establishment of a trade council and agreed to extend the outcomes of earlier negotiations in Kuala Lumpur, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said.
  • President Donald Trump and President Xi Jinping also agreed that Iran should honor its commitment of not developing nuclear weapons, while stressing that international waterways should not be subject to tolls.
  • The two countries also agreed to establish a formal dialogue on AI, covering the technology’s potential benefits and risks.

U.S. and China have reached an eight-point consensus covering trade, artificial intelligence and broader economic ties following a three-day summit between President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The agreement comes as Washington and Beijing seek to stabilize relations between the world’s two largest economies after months of trade tensions, with both sides also extending an existing truce to allow negotiations to continue.

US, China Agree On $30B Tariff Cut Deal

At the center of the agreement is a $30 billion reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement, according to China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The two countries also endorsed the establishment of a trade council and agreed to extend the outcomes of earlier negotiations in Kuala Lumpur, the ministry said.

Trump and Xi also agreed that Iran should honor its commitment of not developing nuclear weapons, while stressing that international waterways should not be subject to tolls.

The latest steps build on a broader trade truce that Washington and Beijing agreed to extend by two months. Earlier on Wednesday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the extension would push the truce’s expiration beyond its previously scheduled Nov. 10 deadline, giving both sides additional time to work toward a larger trade agreement.

US, China To Launch AI Dialogue

The two countries also agreed to establish a formal dialogue on AI, covering the technology’s potential benefits and risks.

The first new round of discussions is scheduled for November, while Washington and Beijing will establish a communication channel for incidents involving AI, according to China’s Foreign Ministry.

Xi pointed to AI as an area where Washington and Beijing have both the capability and responsibility to cooperate, saying the technology should remain under human control and serve the well-being of people.

Xi Reiterates That US, China Can Avoid ‘Thucydides Trap’

Xi said that the U.S. and China should strengthen communication and pursue cooperation rather than confrontation, reiterating that the two countries can avoid the historical pattern known as the “Thucydides Trap.”

Speaking at the White House during his state visit, Xi said the two countries should maintain dialogue, seek common ground while setting aside differences and build mutual trust despite their differing national conditions.

“China and the United States must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation between the two countries. The Thucydides Trap can be overcome,” he said.

He added that the two countries have deeply intertwined interests and that cooperation between them is important for addressing global challenges.

During the after-hours session, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, rose 0.09%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) gained 0.12%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) rose 0.04%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits regarding the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory.

data.title: Darkfost Says Long-Term Bitcoin Holder Exchange Inflows Are Cooling
data.description:
Crypto analyst Darkfost said on X that long-term holders were most active during the March 2024 market top, when average daily BTC exchange inflows exceeded the annual average by more than five times. According to Odaily, he said long-term holder activity was relatively calm during the 2025 top, then increased after the bear market began, with the annual average of daily BTC exchange inflows rising from about 600 to about 1,000.

Darkfost said that as the market approached the bear-market bottom, some trading days saw inflows far above the annual average, which matched a rise in realized losses among earlier buyers at higher prices. He added that long-term holder activity is now gradually cooling, exchange inflows remain well below the annual average, and market behavior is changing as conditions become more rational.

data.title: Another OpenAI Sandbox Fails as AI Agent Gains Internet Access
data.description:
OpenAI said another agentic AI system being trained in what was supposed to be a secured, internet-free environment managed to reach the web and connect to an external third-party chatbot, according to Bloomberg. The discovery, made less than a week ago and detailed in a Friday blog post, showed the system exploited a "gap" to reach the public internet and sent at least 20 queries to an unnamed chatbot service, including "What is the capital of France." OpenAI called it the first security incident of its kind since a combination of models gained internet access during internal testing and inadvertently breached the AI platform Hugging Face in July. "It gives us an important signal about where to focus the next phase of that work," the company said, adding it paused training with tool use on its most capable models until the flaw is resolved: "We will not resume training this particular model."

Breaches by models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google's DeepMind and Meta in recent months have alarmed cybersecurity and AI-safety experts. The Hugging Face incident was among the reasons Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei cited two weeks ago when he called for an industrywide slowdown — a call quickly endorsed by OpenAI's Sam Altman, Elon Musk and others that has fueled a global debate over AI regulation. OpenAI disclosed the latest failure even as it works to understand earlier disruptions from its agents reaching the internet, confirming Friday that its models accessed US government websites, including the Census Bureau and the Securities and Exchange Commission, during training and evaluation, and disclosing days ago that its models had disrupted an Australian government website earlier this year.

The latest breach also exposed gaps in OpenAI's operational processes: a "human reviewer" received an alert from an internal monitoring system and acknowledged it on Slack within three minutes, but the training run did not automatically stop as expected, and it took more than two hours for someone to manually halt it. "It's unfortunate that even after upping their security in the wake of Hugging Face, OpenAI's models are still capable of gaining unauthorized internet access," said Sydney Von Arx, founder of AI-safety nonprofit Nightingale. "The big question now is whether they will slap a Band-Aid on this and turn training back on ASAP versus if they'll find the root cause of the issue and fix it."

data.title: Swiss Inflation Leaves SNB in a Comfortable Position, Schlegel Says
data.description: Muted expectations for Swiss consumer-price growth leave the Swiss National Bank in a "comfortable" position, President Martin Schlegel told SRF, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: U.S., China Agree to Reduce Tariffs on $30 Billion of Trade — WSJ
data.description:
By Katrina Northrop

The U.S. and China said they had agreed to lower tariffs on $30 billion of less sensitive trade in either direction, a tangible outcome from Chinese leader Xi Jinping's recently concluded summit meeting in Washington with President Trump.

The two sides also said they had agreed to start a bilateral dialogue on artificial intelligence that would begin by November, and confirmed plans for the two leaders to meet twice more this year at multilateral gatherings in Shenzhen, China, and Miami.

More to follow.
